scope: Static file inspection of the engine plugin tree. No engine, no asset, no map, no visual acceptance.
purpose: Build 8 near-camera MetaHuman characters WITHOUT any Epic cloud call, by duplicating shipped MetaHuman Creator Core Data presets (which ship already auto-rigged and already carrying high-resolution textures) instead of creating blank characters and paying for RequestAutoRigging + RequestTextureSources. Companion to release_metahuman_enable.py, which takes the blank-character route and is therefore cloud-blocked.

evidence: Windows Credential Manager (cmdkey /list) carries no Epic / EOS / MetaHuman / Unreal target.
HKCU\Software\Epic Games\EOS\MainService is present but empty.

C:/Users/shmue/AppData/Local/UnrealEngine/5.8/Saved/Logs/Unreal.log shows the MetaHuman EOS platform being created but contains no EOS_Auth_Login, PersistentAuth or AccountPortal line: the editor has never attempted a MetaHuman login.

The Epic Games LAUNCHER is signed in (AppData/Local/EpicGamesLauncher/Saved/Data carries the account-id .dat files), but EOSSDKManager.cpp:503-510 disables integrated-platform auth under IsRunningCommandlet(), so a commandlet cannot piggyback that session.
cloud.mechanism: EOS SDK EOS_Auth_Login, not a browser/LoginFlow. MetaHumanCloudAuthentication.cpp FClientState::LoginUsingPersist tries EOS_LCT_PersistentAuth first and escalates to EOS_LCT_AccountPortal on failure. The refresh token is held by the EOS SDK in the Windows Credential Manager for the logged-in Windows user (eos_auth_types.h:42); MetaHuman writes no token of its own to any ini or Saved/ path.
cloud.unattendedTrap: There is NO FApp::IsUnattended() or IsRunningCommandlet() guard anywhere in the MetaHuman auth path. A -unattended commandlet will still attempt LoginUsingAccountPortal, i.e. a GUI flow inside a headless run. ALWAYS pass -NoMetaHumanAccountPortalLoginFallback (parsed at MetaHumanCloudAuthentication.cpp:262) so it fails loudly instead of blocking on an invisible window.
cloud.doNotTrust: UMetaHumanIdentity::IsLoggedInToService() is a dead stub that unconditionally returns true (MetaHumanIdentity.cpp:488-494). There is no honest Python-reachable login probe; the real API lives in namespace UE::MetaHuman::ServiceAuthentication and is not reflected.

textureBudget.sourceMapsDetail: 9 face maps (EFaceTextureType) + 11 body maps (EBodyTextureType), MetaHumanTypes.h:15-50, synthesised at 2048 by default (FMetaHumanCharacterTextureSourceResolutions, MetaHumanCharacterSkin.h:262-297).
textureBudget.mediumBuildCeilingSource: BP_DefaultLegacyPipeline_Medium.uasset name table carries only Res1024/Res2048 (plus one stray Res8192); the exact per-map assignment is Blueprint CDO data and is NOT determinable without opening that Blueprint in the editor.
textureBudget.statedBudget: Plan 60-110 MB of unique texture per built character at OPTIMIZED/MEDIUM, plus a shared Common folder. Eight near-camera characters is therefore roughly 0.5-0.9 GB of unique character texture on an 8 GB RTX 2070: viable for eight, NOT viable for twenty-four. The 24 PilgrimRigV3 residents stay as the mid and far crowd.

limitations: Nothing in this spec is visual acceptance (AGENTS.md hard rule 7). No character has been seen in the engine.

Preset age and gender are NOT recorded anywhere in the shipped assets. Every age/gender claim in the roster above is a guess to be confirmed by eye, except where the preset's own pre-selected facial hair proves the figure is bearded.

MetaHuman fixes skin, eyes, grooms and facial rig quality. It does NOT fix locomotion: an assembled MetaHuman still needs a locomotion Animation Blueprint, and this project drives residents with a single-node PlayAnimation that cannot cross-fade.
The face rig on a preset is whatever the preset shipped with. This script requests no auto-rig, so it neither improves nor degrades it.

clothing.note: EVERY shipped preset selects /MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Clothing/WI_DefaultGarment, and that asset is a modern crewneck T-shirt and shorts (mesh names DG_bodyShapeB_LOD3_shirt / _shorts, material folder Clothing/Common/Materials/Crewneckt/Male). It is the ONLY outfit that ships in the entire MetaHuman plugin tree. A duplicated preset that is not cleared walks the courtyard in streetwear.
clothing.periodGarments: None ship. A case-insensitive search of the whole MetaHuman plugin tree for robe/tunic/gown/cloak/coat returns only UI icons. Period garments remain modelling work. When a mesh exists, the supported no-Chaos route is the wardrobe slot SlotName="SkeletalMesh" (display name "Skeletal Clothing") declared in MetaHumanCharacter/Config/Editor.ini with ClassesToFilter=("/Script/Engine.SkeletalMesh"), driven by the same try_add_item_from_wardrobe_item / try_add_slot_selection calls. ChaosOutfitAsset + UMetaHumanOutfitPipeline remains the better route for the near dozen because it resizes per body and removes the skin underneath.
